svg.title: 429 lineages with no common trunk
svg.desc: Every independent language lineage Glottolog recognises, drawn as circles sized by number of languages: the largest families are Atlantic-Congo (1,408), Austronesian (1,276), Indo-European (586), Sino-Tibetan (519) and Afro-Asiatic (381); then 232 smaller families, most with five languages or fewer; then 183 isolates. No reconstruction joins any two. Genesis 10 lists seventy nations.
svg.text: Every independent language lineage on earth
The other 232 families, each circle drawn to the same scale
183 isolates: languages with no known relative at all
7,674 first languages, living and recorded extinct, in 246 families and 183 isolates.
Each circle's area is its number of languages (the smallest are enlarged to be seen).
No accepted reconstruction joins any two.
Genesis 10 lists 70 nations, “each with his own language” (Genesis 10:5, ESV).
Glottolog 5.3 (2026). Drawn from its data release, where 238 of the 246 families hold a language in this count.
After the manner of Clarence Larkin · the-way.lewy.au
